text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Justice Minister Sevket Kazan says a request for the lifting of former interior minister Mehmet Agar's parliamentary immunity will be sent to parliament. Agar resigned in November over a security scandal.
- Main opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz is worried that Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan will try to cover up a scandal of ties between the state and organised crime.
- The military denies having anything to do with the scandal and says a full investigation should be carried out.
- The suspension from duty of Istanbul's police chief is causing friction between the coalition partners.
- Intellengence service report reveals that government MP Sedat Bucak is involved in illegal financial dealings.
- Credit card authorities say they see no problem in Turkish credits cards being accepted abroad.
- Yilmaz hands documents to President Suleyman Demirel that cast light on the scandal.
- Number of those killed in traffic accidents dropped to 4,908 in the first 11 months of 1996 compared to 6,004 last year.
